ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n greater than 1
k ranges over integers with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n
the floor function is applied to real numbers (so it is always defined)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Define f(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Determine the set of real numbers x for which f(x) is a global maximum among all real y, and determine the value of that global maximum.
quantifier_order: for a given integer n greater than 1
find real x such that for all real y, expression at x is at least the expression at y
and there exists at least one real x achieving that maximal value

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.parent_proof_nl:
Let n>1 and let r be real with (n-1)/n <= r < 1. We show that every floor term in the definition of f_n(r) is determined explicitly.

Fix k with 1 <= k <= n. From r >= (n-1)/n we get kr >= k(n-1)/n. Since k <= n, we have k(n-1)/n >= k-1. Also r < 1 implies kr < k. Therefore
k-1 <= kr < k.
Hence floor(k r) = k-1 for every k=1,2,...,n.

In particular, floor(nr)=n-1, and
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (1 - 1/k) = n - H_n,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Therefore
f_n(r) = floor(nr) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = (n-1) - (n - H_n) = H_n - 1.
This is exactly the desired identity.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
in the definition of H_n, k ranges over integers from 1 to n
in the definition of f_n(x), x is a real number so that floor(n*x) and floor(k*x) are well-defined
parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every natural number n greater than 1, define H_n as the sum from k = 1 to n of 1 divided by k, and define f_n on real numbers by f_n(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Then for every real number r with (n minus 1) divided by n less than or equal to r and r less than 1, it holds that f_n(r) equals H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all natural numbers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with (n-1)/n <= r and r < 1
